source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.original_treatment_name: Celtis laevigata Willd. var. reticulata Torr.

morphology_documented.growth_habit: Small to medium-large tree (Celtis laevigata broad concept); variety-specific height not documented
morphology_documented.bark: Gray, smooth or warty-roughened (broad Celtis laevigata treatment)
morphology_documented.leaves: Leaf blades 2–4.5(–7) cm, thick and stiff; dark green above, pale beneath with prominent raised reticulate veins and pubescence; upper surface usually harshly scabrous, base cordate to sometimes oblique, mature apex obtuse to acute
morphology_documented.flowers: Small; both staminate and perfect flowers (broad C. laevigata account)
morphology_documented.fruit: Rounded drupes usually (5–)8–10 mm diameter, dark red to reddish black on pedicels longer than subtending petioles
morphology_documented.habitat: Regional distribution mostly western half of Texas; precise habitat for this variety not independently stated

source_scope_note: Species vs. genus or key-level characters distinguished in each entry. No missing traits inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Diggs 1999 recognizes C. laevigata var. reticulata; specifically notes Sherman-Broyles et al. 1997 recognize it as separate species C. reticulata
Historical Ulmaceae family now routed to Cannabaceae
Do not generalize variation in var. texana to this current species
preservation: Additive record; original species.json, media, credits and galleries unchanged
